passages.title: Section I: Use of English
passages.content:
Here's a common scenario that any number of entrepreneurs face today: you're the CEO of a small business, and though you're making a nice [1], you need to find a way to take it to the next level. What you need to do is [2] growth by establishing a growth team. A growth team is made up of members from different departments within your company, and it harnesses the power of collaboration to focus [3] on finding ways to grow.

Let's look at a real-world [4]. Prior to forming a growth team, the software company BitTorrent had 50 employees working in the [5] departments of engineering, marketing and product development. This brought them good results until 2012, when their growth plateaued. The [6] was that too many customers were using the basic, free version of their product. And [7] improvements to the premium, paid version, few people were making the upgrade.

Things changed, [8], when an innovative project-marketing manager came aboard, [9] a growth team and sparked the kind of [10] perspective they needed. By looking at engineering issues from a marketing point of view, it became clear that the [11] of upgrades wasn't due to a quality issue. Most customers were simply unaware of the premium version and what it offered.

Armed with this [12], the marketing and engineering teams joined forces to raise awareness by prominently [13] the premium version to users of the free version. [14], upgrades skyrocketed, and revenue increased by 92 percent.

But in order for your growth team to succeed, it needs to have a strong leader. It needs someone who can [15] the interdisciplinary team and keep them on course for improvement. This leader will [16] the target area, set clear goals and establish a time frame for the [17] of these goals.

passages.title: Section II: Reading Comprehension Part A - Text 1
passages.content:
In the quest for the perfect lawn, homeowners across the country are taking a shortcut—and it is the environment that is paying the price. About eight million square metres of plastic grass is sold each year but opposition has now spread to the highest gardening circles. The Chelsea Flower Show has banned fake grass from this year's event, declaring it to be not part of its ethos. The Royal Horticultural Society (RHS), which runs the annual show in west London, says it has introduced the ban because of the damage plastic grass does to the environment and biodiversity.

Ed Horne, of the RHS, said: "We launched our sustainability strategy last year and fake grass is just not in line with our ethos and views on plastic. We recommend using real grass because of its environmental benefits, which include supporting wildlife, alleviating flooding and cooling the environment."

The RHS's decision comes as campaigners try to raise awareness of the problems fake grass causes. A Twitter account, which claims to "cut through the greenwash" of artificial grass, already has more than 20,000 followers. It is trying to encourage people to sign two petitions, one calling for a ban on the sale of plastic grass and another calling for an "ecological damage" tax on such lawns. They have gathered 7,276 and 11,282 signatures.

However, supporters of fake grass point out that there is also an environmental impact with natural lawns, which need mowing and therefore usually consume electricity or petrol. The industry also points out that real grass requires considerable amounts of water, weed killer or other treatments and that people who lay fake grass tend to use their garden more. The industry also claims that people who lay fake grass spend an average of £500 on trees or shrubs for their garden, which provides habitat for insects.

In response to another petition last year about banning fake lawns, which gathered 30,000 signatures, the government responded that it has "no plans to ban the use of artificial grass."

It added: "We prefer to help people and organizations make the right choice rather than legislating on such matters. However, the use of artificial grass must comply with the legal and policy safeguards in place to protect biodiversity and ensure sustainable drainage, while measures such as the strengthened biodiversity duty should serve to encourage public authorities to consider sustainable alternatives."

passages.title: Section II: Reading Comprehension Part A - Text 2
passages.content:
It's easy to dismiss as absurd the federal government's ideas for plugging the chronic funding gap of our national parks. Can anyone really think it's a good idea to allow Amazon deliveries to your tent in Yosemite or food trucks to line up under the redwood trees at Sequoia National Park?

But the government is right about one thing: U.S. national parks are in crisis. Collectively, they have a maintenance backlog of more than $12 billion. Roads, trails, restrooms, visitor centers and other infrastructure are crumbling.

But privatizing and commercializing the campgrounds would not be a cure-all. Campgrounds are a tiny portion of the overall infrastructure backlog, and businesses in the parks hand over, on average, only about 5% of their revenues to the National Park Service.

Moreover, increased privatization would certainly undercut one of the major reasons why 300 million visitors come to the parks each year: to enjoy nature and get a break from the commercial drumbeat that overwhelms daily life.

The real problem is that the parks have been chronically starved of funding. We conducted a comprehensive survey examining how U.S. residents view their national parks, and we found that Americans place a very high value on them—whether or not they actually visit them. The peer-reviewed economic survey of 700 U.S. taxpayers, conducted by mail and internet, also found that people would be willing to pay a significant amount of money to make sure the parks and their programs are kept intact. Some 81% of respondents said they would be willing to pay additional taxes for the next 10 years to avoid any cuts to the national parks.

The national parks provide great value to U.S. residents both as places to escape and as symbols of nature. On top of this, they produce value from their extensive educational programs, their positive impact on the climate through carbon sequestration, their contribution to our cultural and artistic life, and of course through tourism. The parks also help keep America's past alive, working with thousands of local jurisdictions around the country to protect historical sites—including Ellis Island and Gettysburg—and to bring the stories of these places to life.

The parks do all this on a shoestring. Congress allocates only $3 billion a year to the national park system—an amount that has been flat since 2001 (in inflation-adjusted dollars) with the exception of a onetime boost in 2009 as part of the Obama stimulus package. Meanwhile, the number of annual visitors has increased by more than 50% since 1980, and now stands at 330 million visitors per year.

passages.title: Section II: Reading Comprehension Part A - Text 3
passages.content:
The Internet may be changing merely what we remember, not our capacity to do so, suggests Columbia University psychology professor Betsy Sparrow. In 2011, Sparrow led a study in which participants were asked to record 40 factoids in a computer ("an ostrich's eye is bigger than its brain," for example). Half of the participants were told the information would be erased, while the other half were told it would be saved. Guess what? The latter group made no effort to recall the information when quizzed on it later, because they knew they could find it on their computers. In the same study, a group was asked to remember both the information and the folders it was stored in. They didn't remember the information, but they remembered how to find the folders. In other words, human memory is not deteriorating but "adapting to new communications technology," Sparrow says.

In a very practical way, the Internet is becoming an external hard drive for our memories, a process known as "cognitive offloading." Traditionally, this role was fulfilled by data banks, libraries, and other humans. Your father may never remember birthdays because your mother does, for instance. Some worry that this is having a destructive effect on society, but Sparrow sees an upside. Perhaps, she suggests, the trend will change our approach to learning from a focus on individual facts and memorization to an emphasis on more conceptual thinking—something that is not available on the Internet. "I personally have never seen all that much intellectual value in memorizing things," Sparrow says, adding that we haven't lost our ability to do it.

Still other experts say it's too soon to understand how the Internet affects our brains. "There is no experimental evidence showing that it interferes with our ability to focus, for instance," wrote psychologists Christopher Chabris and Daniel J. Simons. And surfing the web exercised the brain more than reading did among computer-savvy older adults in a 2008 study involving 24 participants at the Semel Institute for Neuroscience and Human Behavior at the University of California, Los Angeles.

"There may be costs associated with our increased reliance on the Internet, but I'd have to imagine that overall the benefits are going to outweigh those costs," observes psychology professor Benjamin Storm. "It seems pretty clear that memory is changing, but is it changing for the better? At this point, we don't know."

passages.title: Section II: Reading Comprehension Part A - Text 4
passages.content:
Teenagers are paradoxical. That's a mild and detached way of saying something that parents often express with considerably stronger language. But the paradox is scientific as well as personal. In adolescence, helpless and dependent children who have relied on grown-ups for just about everything become independent people who can take care of themselves and help each other. At the same time, once cheerful and compliant children become rebellious teenage risk-takers.

A new study published in the journal Child Development, by Eveline Crone of the University of Leiden and colleagues, suggests that the positive and negative sides of teenagers go hand in hand. The study is part of a new wave of thinking about adolescence. For a long time, scientists and policy makers concentrated on the idea that teenagers were a problem that needed to be solved. The new work emphasizes that adolescence is a time of opportunity as well as risk.

The researchers studied "prosocial" and rebellious traits in more than 200 children and young adults, ranging from 11 to 28 years old. The participants filled out questionnaires about how often they did things that were altruistic and positive, like sacrificing their own interests to help a friend, or rebellious and negative, like getting drunk or staying out late.

Other studies have shown that rebellious behavior increases as you become a teenager and then fades away as you grow older. But the new study shows that, interestingly, the same pattern holds for prosocial behavior. Teenagers were more likely than younger children or adults to report that they did things like unselfishly help a friend.

Most significantly, there was a positive correlation between prosociality and rebelliousness. The teenagers who were more rebellious were also more likely to help others. The good and bad sides of adolescence seem to develop together.

Is there some common factor that underlies these apparently contradictory developments? One idea is that teenage behavior is related to what researchers call "reward sensitivity." Decision-making always involves balancing rewards and risks, benefits and costs. "Reward sensitivity" measures how much reward it takes to outweigh risk.

Teenagers are particularly sensitive to social rewards—winning the game, impressing a new friend, getting that boy to notice you. Reward sensitivity, like prosocial behavior and risk-taking, seems to go up in adolescence and then down again as we age. Somehow, when you hit 30, the chance that something exciting and new will happen at that party just doesn't seem to outweigh the effort of getting up off the couch.

passages.title: Section II: Reading Comprehension Part B
passages.content:
Net-Zero Rules Set to Send Cost of New Homes and Extensions Soaring

[I] New building regulations aimed at improving energy efficiency are set to increase the price of new homes, as well as those of extensions and loft conversions on existing ones.

[II] The rules, which came into effect on Wednesday in England, are part of government plans to reduce the UK's carbon emissions to net zero by 2050. They set new standards for ventilation, energy efficiency and heating, and state that new residential buildings must have charging points for electric vehicles.

[III] The moves are the most significant change to building regulations in years, and industry experts say they will inevitably lead to higher prices at a time when a shortage of materials and high labour costs are already driving up bills.

[IV] Brian Berry, chief executive of the Federation of Master Builders, says the measures will require new materials, testing methods, products and systems to be installed. "All this comes at an increased cost during a time when prices are already sky high. Inevitably, consumers will have to pay more," he says.

[V] Gareth Belsham, of surveyors Naismiths, says people who are upgrading, or extending their home, will be directly affected. "The biggest changes relate to heating and insulation," he explains. "There are new rules concerning the amount of glazing used in extensions, and any new windows or doors must be highly insulated."

[VI] Windows and doors will have to adhere to higher standards, while there are new limits on the amount of glazing you can have to reduce unwanted heat from the sun.

[VII] Thomas Goodman, of MyJobQuote, says this will bring in new restrictions for extensions. "Glazing on windows, doors and roof lights must cover no more than 25% of the floor area to prevent heat loss," he says.

[VIII] As the rules came into effect last Wednesday, property developers were rushing to file plans just before the deadline. Any plans submitted before that date are considered to be under the previous rules, and can go ahead as long as work starts before 15 June next year.

[IX] Builders which have costed projects, but have not filed the paperwork, may need to go back and submit fresh estimates, says Marcus Jefford of Build Aviator.

[X] Materials prices are already up 25% in the last two years. How much overall prices will increase as a result of the rule changes is not clear. "Whilst admirable in their intentions, they will add to the cost of housebuilding at a time when many already feel that they are priced out of homeownership," says Jonathan Rolande of the National Association of Property Buyers. "An average extension will probably see around £3,000 additional cost thanks to the new regs."

[XI] John Kelly, a construction lawyer at Freeths law firm, believes prices will eventually come down. But not in the immediate future. "As the marketplace adapts to the new requirements, and the technologies that support them, the scaling up of these technologies will eventually bring costs down, but in the short term, we will all have to pay the price of the necessary transition," he says.

[XII] However, the long-term effects of the changes will be more comfortable and energy-efficient homes, adds Andrew Mellor, of PRP architects. "Homeowners will probably recoup that cost over time in energy bill savings. It will obviously be very volatile at the moment, but they will have that benefit over time."

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [1] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］上下文语义与名词固定搭配。
［解题思路］首句描摹了当今小企业主普遍面临的处境：虽然公司目前“盈利状况良好（making a nice [1]）”，但仍需寻找进一步提升营收的突破口。profit（利润、盈利）构成 make a profit 地道搭配，契合企业管理语境，故选［B］。
［错项排除］［A］purchase（购买、采购）虽可构成 make a purchase，但动作发出者为小企业主而非普通消费者；［C］connection（联系、人脉）与［D］bet（打赌、押注）均偏离商业营收经营语境。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [2] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］上下文语义衔接与动词辨析。
［解题思路］空格句承接首句“提升公司收益”的诉求，指出解决之道在于通过组建增长团队来“优先考虑、重点推进（[2] growth）”业务增长，并与后句“集中力量专注寻找增长途径”构成手段与目的呼应，故选［C］prioritize。
［错项排除］［A］define（下定义）宾语为 growth 而非增长团队，组建团队不能用来定义增长；［B］predict（预测）仅止步于预判数字，未体现主动推动业绩增长的实际行动；［D］appreciate（欣赏、感激）不合动宾逻辑。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [3] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］句内语义与副词词义辨析。
［解题思路］增长团队汇聚跨部门成员并借用协作力量，目的就是为了“专心致志、专门地（[3]）专注于寻找增长方法”。exclusively（排他地、专门地）呼应上句 prioritize growth，体现整合全公司力量攻关核心目标，故选［A］。
［错项排除］［B］temporarily（暂时地、临时地）与企业长期寻求业绩突破的战略定位矛盾；［C］potentially（潜在地）及［D］initially（最初、起初）均无法传达增长团队专注且单一的核心职能特征。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [4] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］段际例证逻辑与名词辨析。
［解题思路］第二段首句以 Let's look at a real-world [4]. 引出下文 BitTorrent 公司的真实运营历程，说明公司在成立增长团队前后由停滞转向增长的历程。example（例子、范例）自然承上启下引出具体企业案例，故选［D］。
［错项排除］［A］experiment（科学实验、尝试）侧重主动设计的试验，而下文陈述的是 BitTorrent 公司客观经历的发展沿革；［B］proposal（提议）与［C］debate（辩论）均未在下文案例中有所体现。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [5] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］句内语义与形容词辨析。
［解题思路］空格形容词修饰 departments，指出在组建跨学科增长团队前，50 名员工分别在工程、营销和产品研发等“传统的、常规职能分工下的（[5]）”部门各司其职。traditional 与上段创新的“增长团队”构成鲜明对比，故选［D］。
［错项排除］［A］identical（完全相同的）违背常识，工程、营销与研发职能迥异；［B］marginal（边缘的、次要的）曲解部门地位，三大基础业务部门并非无足轻重；［C］provisional（临时的）意为临时拼凑部门，与“成立多年直至 2012 年才遭遇瓶颈”矛盾。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [6] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］上下文因果衔接与名词辨析。
［解题思路］前句指出旧模式一直运转良好，直到 2012 年增长陷入停滞；紧接着 The [6] was that... 点明导致停滞的症结所在——过多用户始终停留在免费基础版。problem（问题、症结）精准剖析瓶颈根源，故选［D］。
［错项排除］［A］rumor（谣言）若成立则增长停滞并非事实，与下文团队着手解决认知问题相悖；［B］secret（秘诀）通常对应成功经验而非停滞原因；［C］myth（谬论、迷思）无法充当后文客观停滞原因的主语。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [7] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］句内让步转折逻辑与介词辨析。
［解题思路］状语部分提及“对高级付费版进行了诸多改进（improvements to the premium, paid version）”，主句则指出“却依然鲜少有人升级付费”。前后构成强烈的让步转折反差，despite（尽管、虽然）接名词短语引出让步条件，故选［A］。
［错项排除］［B］unlike（不像……）后接对比对象而非具体事实事件；［C］through（通过、凭借）表工具或手段，造成“改进反而导致无人升级”的逻辑谬误；［D］besides（除……之外）表补充递进，无法表现正反落差。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [8] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］段际转折逻辑与逻辑副词辨析。
［解题思路］第二段讲述 BitTorrent 公司自 2012 年起遭遇营收增长瓶颈与免费用户转化停滞，第三段开篇则引入一位富有革新精神的项目营销经理上任并彻底逆转局势。前后两段呈现明显的“困局→转机”强烈反差，however（然而、可是）作插入语置于主从结构间实现段落自然转折，故选［B］。
［错项排除］［A］moreover（此外、而且）引导同向递进补充；［C］therefore（因此、从而）引导顺推因果关系；［D］again（再一次）仅表示重复发生，三者均无法表现“陷入停滞”到“局面彻底改观”的逆转态势。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [9] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］上下文语义呼应与动词辨析。
［解题思路］革新营销经理上任后采取了关键行动：先是“[9] a growth team”，随后激发出全新视角。回溯前两段可知，此前公司并未设立过增长团队，因此此处应为“创建、组建（created）”该团队，并与“激发出全新视角”形成动作顺承，故选［B］。
［错项排除］［A］inspected（视察、检查）前提是团队业已存在，与前文“组建增长团队之前（before a growth team existed）”直接冲突；［C］expanded（扩大）与［D］reformed（改革）同样预设该团队早已设立，不合文意。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [10] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］上下文语义与形容词辨析。
［解题思路］前文强调该经理“富有革新精神（innovative）”，随后团队“以营销视角审视原本属于工程范畴的困扰”。这正表明增长团队激发了公司急需的“崭新的、清新的（[10]）”视角，打破单一部门壁垒，故选［C］fresh。
［错项排除］［A］cultural（文化的）在文中并无企业文化建设的相关佐证；［B］objective（客观的）虽无明显错误但未能呼应“从营销跨界审视工程难题”的新颖视角；［D］personal（个人的）与跨部门集体协作宗旨相悖。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [11] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］上下文语义衔接与名词辨析。
［解题思路］从全新视角审视后发现，用户升级的“[11]（匮乏、不足）”并非源于产品质量缺陷，而是大部分客户根本不知道高级版的存在。lack 与前段 few people were making the upgrade 精准呼应，故选［C］。
［错项排除］［A］end（终结）暗示升级已彻底停止，与下文转机及升级暴涨相悖；［B］burden（负担）与文意“无人升级”相反；［D］decrease（下降）若无基数对比易生歧义，原文强调长期以来鲜有人知、升级严重不足而非单纯速率下跌。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [12] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］段际指代衔接与名词词义辨析。
［解题思路］第四段首句 Armed with this [12] 中，this 回指第三段刚刚揭示的深层症结（客户压根不知晓付费版及其功能）。掌握这一“深刻认识、洞见（insight）”后，营销与工程团队联手精准破局，故选［D］。
［错项排除］［A］policy（政策、方针）、［B］suggestion（建议）以及［C］purpose（目的）在第三段中均未提及；前段着力于视角的转换与问题根源的洞察，故只有 insight 严丝合缝。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [13] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］句内语义与动宾搭配。
［解题思路］针对“客户根本不知道高级付费版”的认知盲区，营销与工程团队联手向免费基础版用户突出地“[13]（推广、宣传）”高级版（prominently promoting the premium version to users of the free version），以提升市场知晓度，故选［C］。
［错项排除］［A］contributing（捐赠）多指慈善或非营利性赠送，不适用商业软件推销；［B］allocating（分配、划拨）常用于分配资源份额；［D］transferring（转移）不能与推广认知语境匹配。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [14] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］句间因果逻辑与短语辨析。
［解题思路］前句指出两部门联手大举向免费用户推广高级版、提高产品知名度，紧接空格句写明市场回报：“升级量呈爆炸式增长，营收跃升 92%”。前因后果逻辑链条明确，As a result（结果、因此）顺理成章，故选［A］。
［错项排除］［B］At any rate（无论如何）常用于让步后强调重点；［C］By the way（顺便提一句）用于引出偏离主线的话题；［D］In a sense（在某种意义上）表限定程度，均不表因果。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [15] in the passage:

［错项排除］［B］finance（为……提供资金）偏离领导者日常统筹职责；［C］follow（追随）主被动关系颠倒；［D］choose（挑选）在团队既已建成的语境下无法延续“领导团队持续进步”的动作连贯性。

［错项排除］［A］share（分享、分担）削弱领导者明确方向的职责；［C］divide（划分、分割）容易导致跨部门重新割裂；［D］broaden（拓宽）与聚焦重点发力（target area）矛盾。

［错项排除］［A］announcement（宣布）是一瞬间即可完成的公告动作，无需设置跨度时间框架；［B］assessment（评估）与［C］adjustment（调整）均非“设定清晰目标”后规划时间表的终极指向。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [19] in the passage:

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [20] in the passage:

［精准定位］根据题干关键词 RHS 及 plastic grass 定位至第一段末句及第二段。文中明确指出皇家园艺学会（RHS）禁止人造草坪参加切尔西花展，原因正是塑料草坪对环境与生物多样性造成破坏（the damage plastic grass does to the environment and biodiversity / Artificial grass... is just not in line with our ethos）。由此可知 RHS 认为塑料草坪对环境有害，故［A］is harmful to the environment 正确。

questions.stem: The petitions mentioned in Paragraph 3 reveal the campaigners'
questions.explanation:

［精准定位］根据题干关键词 petitions 与 Paragraph 3 定位至第三段。该段指出，宣传反对人造草坪的活动者发起两份请愿书——分别呼吁“禁止出售塑料草坪”以及“对此类草坪征收生态破坏税”，且目前已征集大量签名。这种明确寻求禁售和征税的做法直接揭示了环保活动人士对使用人造草坪的抵制，故［B］resistance to fake grass use 正确。
［错项排除］［A］对 RHS 感到失望与文意相反，请愿活动恰恰与 RHS 的禁展立场站在同一阵线；［C］对拟议征税感到愤怒正反颠倒，税收是请愿者主动呼吁出台的惩罚举措；［D］对天然草坪供应的担忧属无中生有。

questions.stem: What problem are U.S. national parks faced with?
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］细节事实题（困境梳理定位）。
［精准定位］根据题干提问美国国家公园面临的问题，定位至第二段。该段明确指出美国国家公园正陷入危机，累积了高达逾 120 亿美元的维护积压账目（a maintenance backlog of more than $12 billion），道路、步道、洗手间、游客中心及其他各类基础设施正在坍塌毁坏（crumbling）。可见核心困境在于基础设施维护严重不足、破败不堪，故［D］Poorly maintained infrastructure 正确。
［错项排除］［A］商业利润下滑在第三段仅提及公园内商业企业上交约 5% 收入，并非企业利润下降；［B］商业化程度不够恰恰是作者批判的政府错误思路，而非实际根源；［C］缺少交通服务偷换了“道路（Roads）破损”的概念。

［错项排除］［B］有助于保护自然违背公园去商业化初衷；［C］带来运营压力及［D］大幅推高入园人数在第四段均未提及。

questions.stem: Sparrow's study shows that with the Internet, the human brain will ________.
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］细节事实题（实验结论定位）。
［精准定位］根据题干关键词 Sparrow's study 与 human brain 定位至第一段。实验中，以为电脑会保存 40 条冷知识的那组受试者事后回忆不起信息内容，却能清楚记住文件存放路径与文件夹名称（They didn't remember the information, but they remembered how to find the folders）。Sparrow 据此得出结论：人类记忆并未退化，而是转而记忆寻找信息的渠道。这表明在互联网时代，人脑正在切换记忆关注的重点，故［C］switch its focus of memory 正确。
［错项排除］［A］详尽分析信息（将 factoids 偷换为深入分析）与［B］高效搜集信息均非该实验观察到的记忆存储偏移结论；［D］延长记忆时长与受试者记不住具体知识点正好相反。

questions.stem: The process of "cognitive offloading" ________.

options.text: enables us to classify trivial facts
options.content: enables us to classify trivial facts

questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］细节事实题（核心概念释义定位）。
［精准定位］根据题干关键词 cognitive offloading 定位至第二段首二句。文中指出，在非常实际的意义上，互联网正在成为人类记忆的“外接硬盘（an external hard drive for our memories）”，即所谓的“认知卸载（cognitive offloading）”；过去这一外包分担角色通常由数据库、图书馆以及配偶等他人替我们记琐事（如妻子帮丈夫记生日）来承担。可见“认知卸载”把死记硬背的存储任务外包出去，从而切实减轻了人脑的记忆负担，故［D］lessens our memory burdens 正确。
［错项排除］［A］帮助甄别虚假信息未在文中体现；［B］防止记忆力衰退曲解了“并非记忆坏掉，而是外包存储”的客观说明；［C］使我们能对琐碎事实归类将“文件夹存储位置记忆”混同为对零散知识本身加以分类。

questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］人物观点题（积极前景推论）。
［精准定位］根据题干询问 Sparrow 对互联网积极一面的看法，定位至第二段中间部分（but Sparrow sees an upside）。Sparrow 提出，借助认知卸载这一趋势，人类的学习方式或许将迎来变革：从过去聚焦零散事实与死记硬背（from a focus on individual facts and memorization），转向更加注重培养概念性思维能力（to an emphasis on more conceptual thinking）。这直接支持互联网将改革我们的学习方式，故［A］It may reform our learning approach 正确。
［错项排除］［B］对社会产生负面影响实为担心者的观点（Some worry that...），Sparrow 对此持积极态度；［C］提升人类对技术的适应力把“记忆本身正在适应新传播技术（adapting to new communications technology）”篡改为对技术普遍适应能力的提高；［D］干扰概念性思维正好与 Sparrow 主张“更重视概念思维”完全反向。

questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］段落主旨与态度推断题。
［精准定位］根据题干关键词 Paragraph 3 及 how the Internet affects our brains 定位至第三、四段。第三段开篇明确点出“还有其他专家认为，现在要弄清互联网如何影响我们的大脑还为时过早（it's too soon to understand how the Internet affects our brains）”；第四段（末段）末句亦作总结：“似乎很明显记忆正在发生改变，但究竟是在变好还是变坏？在现阶段，我们还不得而知（At this point, we don't know）”。这清晰表明该问题仍需进一步的学术研究，故［A］requires further academic research 正确。
［错项排除］［B］在老年人中最常被研究以偏概全（2008 年那项研究只是受试群体之一）；［C］体现在阅读速度中及［D］取决于上网习惯均属无中生有。

［考点提炼］观点态度与排除法推理（两位学者共同否认的立场）。
［精准定位］综合评估 Sparrow 与 Storm 的全部论述：第一段结尾 Sparrow 明确指出“human memory is not deteriorating（人类记忆力并未衰退）”，第二段末补充说明人类“haven't lost our ability to do it（并未丧失记忆能力）”；末段 Storm 则乐观认为“overall the benefits are going to outweigh those costs（总体上利大于弊）”，且记忆只是在改变形式而非确定变差。由此可见，两位学者都绝不认同“互联网正在削弱我们的记忆力”，故［B］the Internet is weakening our memory 正确。
［错项排除］［A］依赖互联网会有代价是 Storm 亲自承认的前提（There may be costs）；［C］大脑必须锻炼记忆与［D］专注力随年龄下滑均非二人探讨与否定的核心分歧。

questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］细节事实题（首段核心矛盾特征）。
［精准定位］根据题干关键词 Paragraph 1 与 growing into adolescence 定位至第一段。文章开篇点明“Teenagers are paradoxical（青少年充满矛盾）”，随后具体阐释这一双重反差：一方面原本无助且事事依赖成人的孩子变得更加独立、能够自理并互助（independent people）；但与此同时，昔日开朗顺从的孩子却又摇身一变成叛逆爱冒险的少年（rebellious teenage risk-takers）。正负特质并存表明步入青春期的孩子趋于发展出截然相反的性格特征，故［A］develop opposite personality traits 正确。
［错项排除］［B］以不合理方式看世界属于无依据的主观贬低；［C］怀念美好过去及［D］向父母表达爱意均偏离首段对“依赖向独立兼叛逆转型”的剖析。

questions.stem: It can be learned from Paragraph 2 that Crone's study

questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］细节理解题（研究视角突破定位）。
［精准定位］根据题干关键词 Paragraph 2 与 Crone's study 定位至第二段。该段首先指明该研究属于看待青春期新思潮的一部分（a new wave of thinking）；接着与长期以来的传统认知做对比：过去科学家与决策者总把青少年视作“需要解决的麻烦”，而 Crone 的新研究强调青春期“既是充满风险也是蕴含机遇的时期（a time of opportunity as well as risk）”。显然该研究打破成见，提供了认识青春期的全新视角，故［C］provides a new insight into adolescence 正确。
［错项排除］［A］探索青少年社会责任以偏概全，下文调查涵盖助人与叛逆两方面；［B］审视青少年情绪问题及［D］突出消极叛逆行为恰是传统旧观念的局限所在，并非克罗恩研究的突破点。

questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］细节事实题（实验主要发现定位）。
［精准定位］根据题干关键词 Crone's study 与 prosocial behavior 定位至第四段。文中提到既有研究表明叛逆行为随青春期升高并在成年后消退；紧接着 Crone 的新研究显示，令人惊讶的是，亲社会行为遵循完全相同的变化模式（the same pattern holds for prosocial behavior）——青少年比幼童或成年人更倾向于报告自己做过无私助友之举。这表明亲社会行为往往在青春期达到峰值，故［D］It tends to peak in adolescence 正确。
［错项排除］［A］源于合作愿望、［B］通过教育培养及［C］受家庭影响在第四段对正相关性与变化曲线的论述中均未曾提及。

questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］细节推断题（行为动机深度剖析）。
［精准定位］根据题干关键词 last two paragraphs 与 teenagers 定位至最后两段。倒数第二段归因于“回报敏感性（reward sensitivity）”，末段首句更是直言青少年“对社会性回报尤为敏感（particularly sensitive to social rewards）”，如赢得比赛、给新朋友留下好印象、吸引心仪异性注意等。这鲜明说明青少年非常看重来自同伴和周围人的社会认可，故［B］care a lot about social recognition 正确。
［错项排除］［A］过度强调自己对他人的影响混淆因果，青少年是在意他人评价与认可而非高估自身影响力；［C］对未来感到焦虑及［D］努力过快乐生活均偏离“对社交赞赏敏感度峰值”的主题。

questions.stem: What is the text mainly about?
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］主旨大意题（全篇行文脉络总结）。
［精准定位］文章首段即开门见山提出“Teenagers are paradoxical”的核心谜题：青少年同时展现无私独立与叛逆冒险的两面；第二至五段引用 Crone 团队对 200 多名青少年的调查，实证亲社会行为与叛逆行径竟呈正相关；最后两段从心理学机制“社交回报敏感度”揭示二者共存并随年龄回落的内在原因。全文始终围绕“青少年为何自我矛盾”层层解密，故［A］Why teenagers are self-contradictory 正确。
［错项排除］［B］为何青少年对风险敏感仅涉及最后两段的解释概念，且文中重在说明他们看重社交回报压倒风险而非单纯怕风险；［C］如何培养亲社会性及［D］如何变得独立均以偏概全。
